label: Vassal count
summary: Whether the number of vassals the character has is as high as the given comparison.
details: Barons are not counted. Write it as a comparison, for example `vassal_count >= 3`. Vanilla also compares it with `vassal_limit`.

label: Vassal limit
summary: Whether the character's vassal limit is as big as the given comparison.
details: Write it as a comparison, for example `vassal_limit > 5`. The input shows no vanilla use of it. To compare the limit with how many vassals they hold, see `vassal_count` and `vassal_limit_available`.

label: Free vassal slots
summary: Whether the character has as much room left under their vassal limit as the given comparison.
details: A negative value means the character is above their limit, so `vassal_limit_available < 0` finds over-limit characters. Vanilla mostly checks `> 0` (room left) or `<= 0` (no room).

label: Vassal limit used
summary: Whether the character's vassal count, compared to their vassal limit, is as big as the given comparison.
details: The game's documentation does not say if the value is written as a percentage (50) or a fraction (0.5), and vanilla does not use it in the input.

label: Wanderer perk points
summary: Whether the character has as many perk points available as the given comparison.
details: The key's name points to the wanderer lifestyle, but the game's documentation only says "perk points available". Write it as a comparison.

label: Wanderer perks owned
summary: Whether the number of wanderer lifestyle perks the character has is as high as the given comparison.
details: Write it as a comparison, for example `>= 3`.

label: Wanderer perks unlockable
summary: Whether the number of wanderer lifestyle perks the character could unlock right now is as high as the given comparison.
details: A perk counts when the character has its parent perks and its `can_be_picked` condition is met. Perk points are not checked, so a character with no points can still count perks here.

label: Wanderer lifestyle XP
summary: A number about the character's wanderer lifestyle, compared as written; the game's documentation does not say what is counted.
details: The game's documentation for this key is a copy of the perk points text, so it does not say what is counted. Going by the name, it is probably the lifestyle's experience, but that is a guess.

label: War chest gold
summary: Whether the character has enough gold for the AI's "war chest" budget, compared as written.
details: The game's documentation names it an AI category, a gold budget the AI keeps for war. Vanilla compares it with named values such as `war_chest_gold_maximum`, a halved or quarter version of it, or a small fixed number.

label: War chest gold target
summary: Whether the size the character's gold war chest is meant to reach is as big as the given comparison.
details: This is the target size of the AI's gold budget for war, not what the character holds now. Compare the held amount with `war_chest_gold`.

label: War chest treasury
summary: Whether the character has enough treasury for the AI's "war chest" budget, compared as written.
details: The treasury is a money pool some rulers use instead of plain gold (the game's documentation of the combined check says "if they don't use treasury"). Vanilla compares it with `war_chest_treasury_maximum`, a halved version, a cautious minimum or a small fixed number.

label: War chest treasury target
summary: Whether the size the character's treasury war chest is meant to reach is as big as the given comparison.
details: This is the target size of the AI's treasury budget for war, not what the character holds now. Compare the held amount with `war_chest_treasury`.

label: War chest treasury or gold
summary: Whether the character has enough treasury for the AI's war chest, or enough gold if they do not use a treasury.
details: It combines the treasury and gold checks: it looks at treasury for characters who use one and at gold for the rest.

label: War contribution
summary: Whether a given character has contributed to the war as much as the comparison says.
details: Runs on a war. `target` is the character whose contribution is checked; `value` is the comparison on the contribution amount. Vanilla mostly writes `value > 0`, and sometimes larger amounts like 100 or 1000.

fields.name: target
fields.text: The character whose contribution is checked.

fields.name: value
fields.text: The comparison on how much they contributed.
fields.values: a comparison such as `> 100`, with a number or script value

label: War length in days
summary: Whether the war has been going on for as many days as the given comparison.
details: Runs on a war. The value is in days, so a year is 365. Vanilla uses it for thresholds like 30, 365, 730 and 9125 days.

label: Warfare legacy perks
summary: Whether the dynasty has as many perks as the given comparison, in what the game's documentation calls "the lifestyle".
details: Runs on a dynasty. The game's documentation only says "perks in the lifestyle"; going by the key name it means the dynasty's warfare legacy track, which is an inference.

label: Warscore of a combat
summary: Whether the warscore value of a combat is as high as the given comparison.
details: Runs on a combat (a battle). Warscore is the progress a side makes towards winning the war. Vanilla checks values of 15 and 25.

label: Travel activity completed
summary: Whether the activity tied to this travel plan was completed.
details: Runs on a travel plan. Write `yes` or `no`. The game's documentation says it applies if an activity is or was attached to the plan.

label: Travel activity invalidated
summary: Whether the activity tied to this travel plan was invalidated.
details: Runs on a travel plan. Write `yes` or `no`. The game's documentation says it applies if an activity is or was attached to the plan, and does not explain what invalidates an activity.

label: Was called to war
summary: Whether the given character has already been called into this war.
details: Runs on a war. The value is the character to check. Vanilla uses `scope:recipient`.

label: Was hostage as child
summary: Whether the character was a hostage when they were a child.
details: Write `yes` or `no`. The game's documentation words it in the past tense, so it is about their history, not their current state.

label: Was preferred heir of
summary: Whether the given character was the preferred heir of the character the check runs on.
details: Write the possible heir as the value, for example `was_preferred_heir = scope:liege`. The documented example puts a character scope there.

label: Weighted conditions sum
summary: Whether the weights of the conditions that are true add up to the required amount.
details: Each inner block is written as `weight = { trigger }`. A block adds its weight only when its trigger is true. The game's documentation says the sum must reach `amount`; vanilla writes `amount = >= 50` style comparisons, so it can be a comparison.

fields.name: amount
fields.text: The sum the true blocks must reach.
fields.values: a number, or a comparison like `>= 50` (as vanilla writes it)

fields.name: <weight>
fields.text: A block named by its weight, holding a trigger. Counts when its trigger is true.
fields.values: a number as the key, with a trigger block

label: Valid for court position
summary: Whether the character could be employed in the court position by the given employer.
details: It only checks; nobody is hired. Vanilla uses it a lot, often for camp officer positions, with the employer given as `root`, `prev` or a saved scope.

fields.name: employer
fields.text: The ruler who would employ the character.

fields.name: court_position
fields.values: a court position key, such as `court_physician_court_position`

label: Yearly treasury income
summary: Whether the character's yearly treasury income is as big as the given comparison.
details: The treasury is a money pool some rulers use instead of plain gold. Compare with a number or script value.

label: Yearly treasury income after development
summary: Whether the character's yearly treasury income, minus Vassal Development expenses, is as big as the given comparison.
details: Compare with `year_character_treasury_income`, which is the figure without that subtraction.

label: Year of birth
summary: Whether the character's birth year fits the given comparison.
details: For example `year_of_birth > 1096` finds characters born after 1096.

label: Yearly gold balance
summary: Whether the character's yearly gold balance is as big as the given comparison.
details: The game's documentation does not define the balance. Going by the name it is the difference between yearly income and expenses, so it can be negative; that is an inference.

label: Yearly expenses
summary: Whether the character's yearly expenses are as big as the given comparison.
details: Compare with a number or script value.

label: Yearly income
summary: Whether the character's yearly income is as big as the given comparison.
details: Compare with a number or script value.

label: Yearly men-at-arms gold cost
summary: Whether the character's yearly gold cost for their men-at-arms, while the troops are not raised, is as big as the given comparison.
details: The game's documentation marks it as the cost of men-at-arms that are not raised.

label: Yearly men-at-arms prestige cost
summary: Whether the character's yearly prestige cost for their men-at-arms, while the troops are not raised, is as big as the given comparison.
details: The game's documentation marks it as the cost of men-at-arms that are not raised.

label: Yearly men-at-arms treasury cost
summary: Whether the character's yearly treasury cost for their men-at-arms, while the troops are not raised, is as big as the given comparison.
details: The game's documentation marks it as the cost of men-at-arms that are not raised.

label: Yearly treasury balance
summary: Whether the character's yearly treasury balance is as big as the given comparison.
details: The game's documentation does not define the balance; compare with a number or script value.

label: Years as diarch
summary: Whether the character has been an active diarch for as many whole years as the given comparison.
details: Only full years count. Vanilla checks 4 and 8 years.

label: Years as ruler
summary: Whether the character has been a ruler for as many years as the given comparison.
details: Gives -1 for a character who is not a ruler, so a check like `< 5` is also true for non-rulers. Vanilla checks 5, 10 and 30 years.

label: Years since game start
summary: Whether the number of years since the game started fits the given comparison.
details: Written as a comparison, for example `years_from_game_start > 5`. Needs no particular scope. Vanilla uses it very often, mostly `>= 1` and `< 1`.

label: Years in diarchy
summary: Whether the character's liege has spent as many whole years in a diarchy as the given comparison.
details: The game's documentation speaks of the liege, so it measures the diarchy of the character's liege, not the character's own. Vanilla checks `>= 2`.

label: Marriage yields alliance
summary: Whether the character would get an alliance with the target character through such a marriage.
details: Vanilla uses it with a block naming a candidate and a target. What the three parameters stand for is not documented, only how vanilla fills them.

fields.name: candidate
fields.text: Used by vanilla for the betrothed who rejects (`scope:rejecting_betrothed`). The game's documentation does not explain it.

fields.name: target
fields.text: Used by vanilla for the owner of the rejected betrothal. The game's documentation does not explain it.

fields.name: target_candidate
fields.text: Used by vanilla for the rejected betrothed. The game's documentation does not explain it.
